fact: Traffic can be directed by police officers, highway workers, and school crossing guards, as well as by signals, signs, and pavement markings. You must obey all of them.
why: People directing traffic can see conditions that a fixed sign or light cannot respond to.

items.q: Which of these must you obey when directing traffic?
choices: Only a police officer in uniform

items.q: You only have to follow traffic signals and signs, not directions from highway workers.

fact: Regulatory signs tell you the law. They are usually black and white, and some are red and white.
why: Knowing the color family helps you recognize a sign as a rule you must follow, even from far away.

items.q: What colors are regulatory signs usually?
choices: Black and white, sometimes red and white

items.q: Regulatory signs are usually black on yellow.

fact: A STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop. Stop at the marked stop line; if there is none, stop before the crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see traffic on the crossing road before entering it.
why: Stopping at the line or before the crosswalk keeps pedestrians safe while still letting you check for cross traffic.
hook: Order to stop: stop line, then crosswalk, then the spot where you can see.
signDesc: Red octagon (8 sides) with white STOP text and white border

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Slow down and yield if needed
Stop only if traffic is coming

items.q: You come to a STOP sign. There is no stop line, but there is a crosswalk on your side of the intersection. Where do you stop?
choices: In the middle of the crosswalk
Right at the edge of the cross street
Wherever you can see best, even past the crosswalk

items.q: At a STOP sign with no stop line and no crosswalk, where should you stop?
choices: Where you can see traffic on the crossing road, before entering it
In the middle of the intersection
Next to the sign post, even if you cannot see

items.q: Where should you stop if there is a clearly marked stop line?
choices: Past the stop line so you can see
Ten feet before the stop line

fact: A YIELD sign means slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first. Stop if you need to, and stop for pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk.
why: Yielding lets traffic flow without a full stop when the way is clear, but others still have the right-of-way.
signDesc: Red and white downward-pointing triangle with red YIELD text

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Slow down and let others go first; stop if needed
Always come to a complete stop

items.q: You reach a YIELD sign. A pedestrian is about to step into the crosswalk in front of you. What should you do?
choices: Stop and wait until the pedestrian has crossed
Keep going because you are already slowing down
Speed up to get through first

items.q: A YIELD sign always requires you to come to a complete stop.
You approach a yield sign and see a car coming on the cross street. What should you do?
choices: Slow down and stop if needed to let it pass
Keep your speed; it must yield to you
Speed up to get ahead of it
Stop fully even after it has passed and wait one minute

fact: A DO NOT ENTER sign means you may not drive onto that road from the direction you are traveling.
why: These signs are often placed where you would be going the wrong way into oncoming traffic.
signDesc: Red circle with a white horizontal bar, white DO NOT ENTER text

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: You may not enter this road from your direction
The road ahead is closed for repairs

items.q: You start to turn onto a ramp and see a red circle sign with a white bar and the words DO NOT ENTER. What should you do?
choices: Do not turn there; find another route
Enter slowly and use your hazard lights
Enter only if no cars are coming
Stop, then continue onto the ramp

fact: The Keep Right sign means the road ahead is divided by an island or barrier. Stay to the right of it.
why: Going to the left of the island would put you in lanes for oncoming traffic.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black arrow curving around the right side of a black island shape

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Stay to the right of the island or barrier ahead
Turn right at the next road

items.q: Ahead you see a raised island splitting the road and a sign with an arrow curving around the right side of it. What should you do?
choices: Drive to the right of the island
Drive to the left of the island

items.q: A Keep Right sign means you must pass to the left of the island ahead.

fact: Some speed signs show a MINIMUM speed. A sign may show both a speed limit and a minimum speed for the same road.
why: Driving far slower than other traffic on fast roads can also cause crashes.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black text MINIMUM SPEED 40

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: The lowest speed you should drive on this road
The speed for night driving only

items.q: A sign reads SPEED LIMIT 50 and MINIMUM 30. What does the 30 mean?
choices: The lowest speed for that road
The speed in a school zone

fact: A speed sign may have a NIGHT plate showing a separate speed limit for nighttime driving.
why: You can see less far at night, so some roads have a lower night limit.
signDesc: Black rectangle with white text NIGHT 45

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: The speed limit that applies at night
A road that is closed at night

items.q: A road has a SPEED LIMIT 50 sign and a NIGHT 45 sign. What is the limit after dark?
A speed sign with a black NIGHT panel shows the speed limit that applies at night.

fact: A No Left Turn sign means you may not turn left at that location. It may use a symbol (left arrow inside a red circle with a slash) or the words NO LEFT TURN.
why: Left turns are banned where they would be unsafe or block traffic.
signDesc: White square, black left-turn arrow inside a red circle with a red diagonal slash

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Left turns are not allowed here

items.q: At an intersection you see a black left arrow inside a red circle with a red slash. You wanted to turn left. What should you do?
choices: Go straight or right and find another route
Turn left only if no cars are coming
Wait for a green light, then turn left

items.q: A red circle with a slash over an arrow means that movement is not allowed.

fact: A No Right Turn sign means you may not turn right at that location. It may be a symbol (right arrow inside a red circle with a slash) or the words NO RIGHT TURN.
why: Right turns may be banned where they would conflict with pedestrians or other traffic.
signDesc: White square, black right-turn arrow inside a red circle with a red diagonal slash

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Right turns are not allowed here

items.q: A white sign reads NO RIGHT TURN. What does it mean?
choices: You may not turn right at this location
You may turn right only on red

fact: A speed limit sign shows the maximum speed allowed on that part of the road under ideal driving conditions.
why: The posted limit is the top speed for good conditions; in bad conditions a safe speed may be lower.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black text SPEED LIMIT 50

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: The highest speed allowed in ideal conditions
The speed you must always drive
A suggested speed for trucks only

items.q: The SPEED LIMIT sign says 50, but heavy rain is making it hard to see. What is true?
choices: 50 is the top speed for ideal conditions; you may need to go slower
You may drive 55 to keep up with traffic
The limit no longer applies in rain

items.q: The number on a SPEED LIMIT sign is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions.

fact: An orange Lane Shift sign means all lanes ahead shift in the direction shown. Stay in your own lane as it shifts.
why: Changing lanes while all lanes are bending can cause side-swipe crashes.
signDesc: Orange diamond with two parallel black arrows that shift to the right then continue up (two-lane reverse curve)

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Lanes shift ahead; stay in your lane

items.q: In a work zone you see an orange sign with two curving arrows side by side. What should you do?
choices: Stay in your lane as it shifts
Stop and wait for a flagger
Speed up to pass before the shift

fact: A lane sign with a left-curving arrow and the word ONLY means traffic in that lane must turn left. A sign showing a left arrow and a straight arrow, with ONLY under the left arrow, means one lane is left turn only and the other goes straight.
why: Drivers need to be in the right lane before the intersection so they do not cut across other lanes.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black left-turn arrow above the word ONLY

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Traffic in this lane must turn left

items.q: You want to go straight, but you are in a lane under a sign with a left arrow and the word ONLY. What must you do?
choices: Turn left, then find another route
Stop and wait to change lanes in the intersection
Back up into the other lane

fact: A No U-Turn sign means you may not turn around (make a U-turn) at that location. It may be a symbol or the words NO U TURN.
why: U-turns are banned where turning around would be dangerous.
signDesc: White square, black U-turn arrow inside a red circle with a red diagonal slash

items.q: What does this sign mean?
Which sign means you may not turn around at this location?
choices: A U-shaped arrow in a red circle with a slash
A yellow diamond with a curved arrow
A white sign with an up arrow and ONLY

items.q: A U-shaped arrow inside a red circle with a slash means you may make a U-turn here.

fact: A lane sign with a right-curving arrow and the word ONLY means traffic in that lane must turn right.
why: Lane signs tell you which lane to be in before you reach the intersection.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black right-turn arrow above the word ONLY

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Traffic in this lane must turn right

items.q: You want to go straight, but your lane has a sign with a right arrow and the word ONLY. What must you do?
choices: Turn right, then find another route
Change lanes in the middle of the intersection
Stop and wait in the lane

fact: A sign with a straight-ahead arrow and the word ONLY means traffic in that lane must go straight.
why: Lane control signs keep turning and through traffic in their own lanes so drivers do not cut across each other.
signDesc: White vertical rectangle, black upward arrow above the word ONLY

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Traffic in this lane must go straight

items.q: You are in a lane under a sign with an up arrow and the word ONLY. What must you do at the intersection?

fact: Never drive around or move barriers or signs to get onto a road that is closed to traffic.
why: Closed roads may have deep holes, missing pavement, or workers that you cannot see.

items.q: A road is blocked by barriers, but you see room to drive around them and it would save time. What should you do?
choices: Use another route; do not go around the barriers
Move a barrier and put it back
Drive through if no workers are visible

items.q: You may move a barrier to get onto a closed road if you put it back afterward.

fact: Work zones are usually marked with orange signs, cones, drums, barricades, or flashing arrow panels. Warning signs in work zones are orange and black.
why: Orange stands out so drivers notice that workers, equipment, and changed lanes are ahead.

items.q: What color are warning signs in a work zone?
Warning signs in a work zone are black on yellow.

fact: An orange flagger sign (the words FLAGGER AHEAD, or a picture of a person holding a flag) means slow down and be prepared to stop for road work ahead.
why: A flagger may stop traffic suddenly to let equipment or workers cross.
signDesc: Orange diamond with black text FLAGGER AHEAD

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Slow down and be ready to stop for road work

items.q: You pass an orange diamond sign that says FLAGGER AHEAD. What should you do next?
choices: Slow down and be ready to stop
Speed up to get through the work zone

items.q: An orange sign with a person holding a flag means you should slow down and be ready to stop.

fact: A ROAD CLOSED sign means the work zone cannot be entered except by authorized people.
why: The road beyond may be unsafe or full of workers and equipment.
signDesc: White horizontal rectangle with black text ROAD CLOSED (the handbook also shows an orange diamond version)

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: No one may enter except authorized personnel
Slow down and proceed with care

items.q: You come to a ROAD CLOSED sign at the start of a work zone. You are not a worker. What should you do?
choices: Do not enter; find another route
Enter if no workers are visible

items.q: You may drive past a ROAD CLOSED sign if you are careful.

fact: A ROAD CLOSED TO THRU TRAFFIC or ROAD CLOSED, LOCAL TRAFFIC ONLY sign means only people who need to stop inside the work zone, such as residents or customers of businesses there, may enter. You may not use it as a route through.
why: Limiting traffic to people with a destination inside keeps the work zone as safe as possible.
signDesc: White horizontal rectangle with black text ROAD CLOSED TO THRU TRAFFIC

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Only drivers with a stop inside the area may enter
No one at all may enter
The road is open to everyone

items.q: You see ROAD CLOSED TO THRU TRAFFIC. You do not live or have business on that road; you just want a shortcut. What should you do?
choices: Follow the detour signs around the work zone
Drive through since it is not fully closed
Drive through slowly with hazard lights on
Wait for workers to wave you through

fact: A plus-shaped (+) warning sign means another road crosses your road ahead. Watch for cross traffic.
why: Cars may enter your path from either side.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with black plus (+) symbol

items.q: What does this sign mean?
What should you watch for when you see a yellow diamond sign with a black plus (+) symbol?

fact: An Open Range sign means livestock may roam freely without fences, and they have the right-of-way.
why: Animals can be on the road at any time, and hitting a large animal is very dangerous.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a black cow symbol (the handbook version adds the words OPEN RANGE)

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Livestock roam freely and have the right-of-way

items.q: You are driving through open range and a cow is standing on the road. What should you do?
choices: Slow down or stop and let the animal move
Flash your lights and speed up

items.q: In an open range area, livestock have the right-of-way.

fact: A Traffic Signal Ahead sign warns of a traffic light ahead. It is used on faster roads or where the light is hard to see. Be ready to stop.
why: At higher speeds you need more distance to stop for a light you cannot see yet.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a traffic light symbol showing red, yellow, and green

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: A traffic light is ahead; be ready to stop
Signals are out; treat as a four-way stop

items.q: Where are Traffic Signal Ahead signs usually used?
choices: On faster roads or where the light is hard to see

fact: A T-shaped warning sign means the road ends ahead at a T intersection, and you will have to turn right or left. Be ready to stop and yield to drivers coming from the other two directions.
why: The road does not continue straight, so you must be ready to stop and turn.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with black T symbol

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Road ends ahead; you must turn right or left

items.q: You see a yellow diamond with a black T shape. What should you expect?
choices: The road ends and you must turn right or left
A road crosses yours and continues
A lane will be added on the left

fact: Most warning signs are black on yellow and diamond shaped. School warning signs may be fluorescent yellow-green. Warning signs alert you to an unexpected condition, so you may need to slow down.
why: A different color and shape from regulatory signs tells you this is a warning about the road, not a law.

items.q: What shape and color are most warning signs?
Most warning signs are black on yellow and diamond shaped.

fact: An Added Lane sign means two roads are joining and a lane is added. Watch for traffic from the left lane moving into the right lane, and check and signal before you move left.
why: Drivers from both roads may try to change lanes at the same time.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with two black arrows side by side, the right arrow curving in, separated by a dashed line

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Two roads join and a lane is added

items.q: You see an Added Lane sign and want to move into the left lane. What should you do first?
choices: Check that it is clear and use your signal
Speed up and move over without signaling

fact: A Lane Ends sign means two lanes will soon become one. Traffic that has to merge must yield.
why: Only one car can fit where the lanes join, so the merging driver must give way.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with two black lines, the right line bending in to meet the left one

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Two lanes become one; merging traffic yields
Road narrows to a one-lane bridge

items.q: You are in the lane that is ending and see the Lane Ends sign. Who must yield?
choices: The car in the continuing lane

items.q: When a lane ends, traffic in the lane that continues must yield to merging drivers.

fact: A Merging Traffic sign tells drivers on the main road to be ready for other vehicles entering their lane.
why: Expecting merging cars lets you adjust speed or space before they arrive.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a black straight arrow and a shorter curved line joining it from the side

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Other vehicles will merge into your lane
A lane is added on the left

items.q: You are on the main road and see a sign showing a line joining your lane from the side. What should you expect?
choices: A lane being added for you

fact: The pentagon (five-sided) school sign means you are near a school area with a crossing. Watch for children. Penalties are increased for breaking school zone speed limits.
why: Children can dart into the road and are hard to see.
signDesc: Fluorescent yellow-green (or yellow) pentagon with two black walking children

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: School area ahead; watch for children

items.q: What shape is the school zone sign?
Penalties for breaking school zone speed limits are higher than in other areas.

fact: A Two-Way Traffic sign (one arrow up, one arrow down) warns that a divided highway is changing to a two-lane road with traffic in both directions.
why: Oncoming traffic will be right next to you with no divider.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with two black vertical arrows, one pointing up and one pointing down

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Two-way traffic ahead on a two-lane road

items.q: You have been on a divided highway and see a sign with one arrow up and one arrow down. What is about to change?
choices: Oncoming traffic will share the road with no divider
A new lane opens on the right

fact: A Divided Highway Begins sign means two-way traffic ahead will be separated by a center strip.
why: You need to stay on the right side once the divider begins.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with black arrows going up on the right and down on the left, split apart by a center island shape

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: A center strip will divide traffic ahead

items.q: What does a Divided Highway Begins sign mean?
choices: Traffic ahead will be separated by a center strip
Oncoming traffic will no longer be separated

fact: A Divided Highway Ends sign means the center strip ends ahead and two-way traffic will no longer be separated. Watch for oncoming cars.
why: Without a divider, oncoming traffic will be close to your lane.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with black arrows that come together after a center island shape ends

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: The center divider ends; watch for oncoming traffic

items.q: You see a sign showing the center island ending and the lanes coming together. What should you watch for?
choices: Oncoming cars close to your lane

items.q: A Divided Highway Ends sign means oncoming traffic will soon be separated from you by a center strip.

fact: A Low Clearance sign shows that the space above the road (such as under a bridge) is very low. The sign lists the height, for example 12'-6".
why: Tall vehicles can hit the structure if they are taller than the clearance.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a height (12'-6") between an up arrow and a down arrow

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Overhead clearance is low; tall vehicles may not fit

items.q: What does a Low Clearance sign warn about?
choices: The space above the road is very low
The speed limit is very low

fact: A Pedestrian Crossing sign warns of people crossing the road. Pedestrians have the right-of-way, and you may have to stop. Some have flashing lights that show a pedestrian is crossing.
why: People on foot have no protection if hit by a car.
signDesc: Yellow or fluorescent yellow-green diamond with a black walking person on a crosswalk

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: People may cross here; be ready to stop

items.q: A pedestrian crossing sign ahead has flashing lights turned on. What does this most likely mean?
choices: A pedestrian is crossing; be ready to stop
You must speed up to clear the crossing

fact: A school sign with a downward arrow plaque below it marks the school crossing itself. Watch for children, slow down, and obey the crossing guard.
why: This is the exact spot where children will be walking across the road.
signDesc: Fluorescent yellow-green pentagon with two walking children, with a small plaque below showing a diagonal downward arrow (W16-7P)

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: This is the school crossing; slow down and watch for children

items.q: You see a school sign with a small arrow plaque under it pointing down to the road. A crossing guard is signaling you to stop. What should you do?
choices: Stop and obey the crossing guard

items.q: School warning signs may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.

fact: A Hill sign warns that the road goes down a steep hill. Check your brakes before going down.
why: On a steep downhill your brakes do more work and your speed can build quickly.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a black truck on a steep downward slope

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Steep downhill ahead; check your brakes

items.q: What should you do before going down the hill shown on a Hill warning sign?

fact: The No Passing Zone sign is a pennant (sideways triangle) on the LEFT side of the road. It warns of a no passing zone for your lane and is used along with a DO NOT PASS sign or pavement markings.
why: Placing it on the left puts it where a driver starting to pass will look.
hook: The pennant sits on the left side of the road, where you would pass.
signDesc: Yellow pennant (sideways triangle pointing right) with black text NO PASSING ZONE

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: No passing zone for your lane

items.q: On which side of the road is the No Passing Zone pennant placed?
The No Passing Zone sign is shaped like a pennant.

fact: A round yellow sign with an X and two R letters gives early warning of a railroad crossing ahead. Be ready to stop before the tracks if a train is coming.
why: Trains cannot stop quickly, so drivers must be the ones to stop.
signDesc: Round yellow sign with a black X and two black letter R's

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Railroad crossing ahead; be ready to stop

items.q: What shape is the railroad advance warning sign?

fact: A Slippery When Wet sign means the road may be slippery in wet weather. Slow down in those conditions.
why: Wet pavement reduces tire grip, making skids more likely.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a black car and wavy skid marks behind it

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: The road can be slippery when wet; slow down

items.q: It is raining and you see a sign with a car and wavy skid marks. What should you do?

fact: An Animal Crossing sign (for example DEER XING) warns you to watch for animals crossing the highway.
why: Animals can appear suddenly, especially where they often cross.
signDesc: Yellow diamond with a black leaping deer and the words DEER XING

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Watch for animals crossing the road

items.q: At dusk you pass a DEER XING (crossing) sign. What should you do?
choices: Watch for animals crossing the road
Speed up to leave the area

fact: The Emergency Notification System sign is posted at or near a railroad crossing. It lists the railroad's phone number and the crossing number so you can report an emergency or broken warning device.
why: The crossing number tells the railroad exactly where the problem is, so it can warn trains.
signDesc: Blue rectangle with white text: REPORT EMERGENCY OR PROBLEM, a phone number, and a CROSSING number

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Call the number shown to report a crossing emergency

items.q: Besides a phone number, what information is on the Emergency Notification System sign?
choices: The crossing number for that location

fact: Guide signs are white on green for directions and distances, white on blue for motorist services, and white on brown for cultural, historical, or scenic places.
why: Color lets you find the kind of information you need at a glance.
hook: Green = go (directions), Blue = services, Brown = parks and history.

items.q: What color is a guide sign for motorist services like gas, food, or a hospital?
What color is a guide sign for a scenic or historic place?
Green guide signs show directions and distances.

fact: Barricades are red and white when permanent and orange and white when temporary. The meaning of the stripes is the same for both colors.
why: Color shows whether the closure is long-term, but drivers follow the same rules either way.

items.q: What do red and white barricades usually mean?
Orange and white barricades give different directions than red and white barricades with the same pattern.

fact: Barricade stripes show which side to pass on: stripes slanting down to the left mean pass on the left; stripes slanting down to the right mean pass on the right. Barricades may have flashing lights, especially at night.
why: The stripes point down toward the open side, like water running downhill.
hook: Follow the stripes downhill to the open side.

items.q: You see a barricade with stripes that slant down toward the right. Which way do you go?
Stripes on a barricade that slant down to the left mean you should pass on the left.

fact: A barricade with stripes forming a V shape means the road is closed and you cannot go any farther.
why: There is no open side to pass on, so the road cannot be used.

items.q: What does a barricade with V-shaped stripes mean?
choices: The road is closed; you cannot continue

items.q: A barricade with V-shaped stripes means you may pass on either side.

fact: The Bicycles May Use Full Lane sign means bicyclists may ride in the middle of the travel lane. It can be used with or instead of sharrows.
why: Some lanes are too narrow for a car and a bike to share side by side.
signDesc: White rectangle with a black bicycle symbol and the words MAY USE FULL LANE

items.q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Bicyclists may ride in the whole travel lane
Bicycles are not allowed on this road

items.q: You see a MAY USE FULL LANE sign and a bicyclist riding in the center of your lane. What should you do?
choices: Stay behind and pass only when it is safe to change lanes
Honk so the cyclist moves right
Squeeze past in the same lane
Drive on the shoulder to pass

fact: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is clear.
why: It works just like a STOP sign.

items.q: What should you do at a flashing red light?
choices: Stop completely, yield, then go when clear
Slow down and go with caution
Stop only if cars are coming
Wait for it to turn green

items.q: A flashing red light means the same as a flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign.

fact: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look carefully for hazards, and go ahead with care.
why: Flashing yellow is often used where there may be cross traffic but a full stop is not required.

items.q: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution
The light is about to turn red

items.q: You must come to a complete stop at a flashing yellow light.

fact: A steady red arrow means you may not turn in that direction until a green or yellow light allows it.
why: The arrow protects traffic or pedestrians moving across your turning path.

items.q: You are in the left-turn lane and the signal shows a steady red arrow. No cars are coming. What should you do?
choices: Wait; do not turn until the signal allows it
Turn if no pedestrians are present
Turn slowly with your signal on

items.q: You may turn on a steady red arrow after stopping if the way is clear.

fact: On a vertical traffic light, red is on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom. On a horizontal light, red is on the far left, yellow in the middle, and green on the far right.
why: A fixed order helps you, including color-blind drivers, tell which light is on by its position.

items.q: On a horizontal traffic light, where is the red light?
On a vertical traffic light, the green light is on top.

fact: A steady red light means come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection. Turning on red is not allowed where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.
why: Red gives the right-of-way to other directions of traffic.

items.q: Where must you stop for a steady red light?
choices: Before the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection

items.q: You are stopped at a steady red light and want to turn. A sign says NO TURN ON RED. What should you do?
choices: Wait for the light to change
Turn if no cars are coming
Turn if a pedestrian waves you on

fact: A steady yellow light warns that the light is about to turn red. If you have not entered the intersection and can stop safely, stop. If you are already in the intersection, keep going and clear it safely.
why: Stopping suddenly inside the intersection would block traffic about to get a green light.

items.q: The light turns yellow just as you are well inside the intersection. What should you do?
choices: Continue and clear the intersection safely
Back up behind the stop line
Speed up to beat other cars

items.q: The light turns yellow while you are still far from the intersection and can stop safely. What should you do?

fact: A steady yellow arrow means the turn signal is about to change. Stop if you have not entered the intersection and can stop safely; if you are already in it, finish your turn and clear it.
why: Your protected time to turn is ending, and other traffic will soon move.

items.q: What does a steady yellow arrow mean?
choices: The turn signal is about to change

items.q: If you are already in the intersection when the turn arrow turns yellow, you should finish your turn and clear the intersection.

items.q: Which signal should you use as you approach your exit from a roundabout?
You should turn on your right turn signal as you approach your exit from a roundabout.

fact: At a thru-turn intersection, direct left turns are not allowed. Go straight through, make a U-turn at the next signal, come back, and turn right.
why: Removing direct left turns keeps traffic moving and avoids left-turn crashes.

items.q: You want to go left at a thru-turn intersection. What should you do?
choices: Go straight, U-turn at the next signal, come back and turn right
Turn left from the right lane
Turn left when the light is yellow
Turn right, then make a U-turn in the median

items.q: At a thru-turn intersection, a left turn is made by going straight, making a U-turn, and then turning right.

fact: Driving too slowly for conditions and blocking the safe flow of traffic also breaks the basic rule, even if you are under the speed limit.
why: Very slow drivers make others brake suddenly or pass in risky places.

items.q: You can break Idaho's basic speed rule by driving too slowly.
The road is dry and clear with a 65 mph limit. You drive 35 mph and a long line of cars builds up behind you. Which is true?
choices: You may be breaking the basic speed rule
You are fine because you are under the limit
The cars behind you must pass on the shoulder
Slow driving is always the safest choice

fact: Idaho's basic rule says you must always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions, such as weather, road surface, traffic, and visibility.
why: A speed limit is the most you may go in good conditions; ice, rain, or heavy traffic can make that speed unsafe.

items.q: The speed limit is 55 mph, but the road is covered in snow. What does the basic rule require?
choices: Drive slower than 55 if needed to be safe
Drive 55 because that is the posted limit
Drive at least 45 to keep up
Turn on hazard lights and drive 55

items.q: If you are at or under the posted speed limit, you can never get a ticket for your speed.
What does Idaho's basic speed rule require?
choices: A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions
Always driving exactly the posted limit
Matching the speed of the car ahead

fact: The maximum speed on Idaho interstates is 75 mph unless a different limit is posted. Where posted, 80 mph may be allowed.
why: Interstates have one-way traffic and limited entrances, so they are built for higher speeds.

items.q: What is the maximum speed on an Idaho interstate when no other limit is posted, in mph?
What is the highest speed that may be allowed on an Idaho interstate where it is posted?
The unposted maximum speed on Idaho interstates is 65 mph.

fact: The maximum speed in any residential, business, or urban district is 35 mph unless a different limit is posted.
why: These areas have many people walking, driveways, and cross streets, so you need time to react.

items.q: What is the maximum speed in a residential or business district when no limit is posted, in mph?
You are driving through a downtown business area and see no speed limit signs. What is the most you may drive?
The default maximum speed in an Idaho residential district is 25 mph.

fact: The maximum speed on Idaho state highways is 65 mph. Where posted, 70 mph may be allowed.
why: State highways often have cross traffic and two-way traffic, so they have lower limits than interstates.

items.q: What is the maximum speed on an Idaho state highway when no higher limit is posted, in mph?
Where posted, what is the highest speed that may be allowed on an Idaho state highway?
State highways in Idaho have the same 75 mph default limit as interstates.

fact: You may not stay in the far left lane in a way that blocks other traffic traveling at a lawful speed.
why: The left lane is for passing; staying in it forces faster drivers to pass on the right.

items.q: You are in the far left lane of a multi-lane highway. Cars going the legal speed are lining up behind you. What should you do?
choices: Move right when it is safe
Stay in the left lane because you are at the limit
Slow down so they will go around you

items.q: It is illegal to stay in the far left lane in a way that blocks traffic moving at a lawful speed.

fact: It is illegal to race, hold a speed contest, or do a speed exhibition on any public road.
why: Racing on public roads puts other drivers and people walking in danger.

items.q: Racing another car on an empty public road at night is legal in Idaho.
Where is it illegal to hold a vehicle race or speed contest?
choices: On any public road, street, or highway

fact: Obey posted speed limits in school zones and work zones. Speeding in a work zone can bring a higher, fixed fine.
why: Children and road workers are close to traffic and have little protection.

items.q: What can happen if you break the speed limit in a marked work zone?
choices: You can get an enhanced, fixed penalty
Nothing extra if no workers are present

items.q: Work zone speed tickets carry the same penalty as any other speeding ticket.
Fines for speeding can be increased in work zones where signs show this.

fact: In business or residential areas, start your turn signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes.
why: 100 feet gives drivers behind you time to slow down before you turn.

items.q: In a residential or business area, at least how many feet before a turn must you signal?
You are driving in a neighborhood and plan to turn right at the next corner. When should you start signaling?
choices: At least 100 feet before the turn
At least 50 feet before the turn
Right as you start the turn
At least 500 feet before the turn

items.q: In a business district, you must signal at least 200 feet before turning.

fact: On freeways and highways, signal for at least five seconds before you turn or change lanes.
why: At high speeds you cover distance fast, so a time-based signal gives others enough warning.

items.q: On a freeway, at least how many seconds should you signal before changing lanes?
You are on the interstate and want to move into the left lane. How long should you signal first?
choices: Signal only as you move over

items.q: On highways, the signal rule is at least 100 feet, the same as in town.

fact: If you plan to turn just past an intersection, signal only after you have passed through the intersection.
why: Signaling earlier could make drivers think you are turning at the intersection itself.

items.q: You want to turn into a driveway just past a cross street. When should you signal?
choices: After you pass through the intersection
Only once you are in the driveway
You do not need to signal for a driveway

items.q: Why wait to signal when turning just beyond an intersection?
choices: So other drivers do not think you are turning at the intersection
Because signals are not needed for driveways

fact: Use your turn signal when you change lanes, pass, turn, exit a roundabout, enter or leave a freeway, pull away from a curb, or pull over to the side of the road.
why: Signals tell others what you are about to do so they can react in time.

items.q: You are parked along a street and are ready to pull into traffic. What should you do?
choices: Signal, check traffic, and pull out when safe
Turn on your hazard lights and pull out

items.q: You must signal when pulling away from a parked position into traffic.

fact: When two lanes can turn left, the left lane must turn left, while the right lane may turn left or go straight. Stay in your own lane until the turn is finished.
why: Staying in your lane through the turn keeps you from hitting a car turning beside you.

items.q: You are turning left from the right of two lanes that can both turn left. A car is turning beside you on the left. What should you do?
choices: Stay in your lane until you finish the turn
Drift into the left lane during the turn
Speed up to get in front of the other car
Stop in the middle of the intersection

items.q: Vehicles in the left lane may go straight instead of turning left.

fact: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you may turn on a steady red light after stopping and yielding to cross-traffic, unless a sign says not to.
why: Like a right on red, this turn does not cross any oncoming lanes.

items.q: You are on a one-way street at a steady red light. You want to turn left onto another one-way street going left. No sign forbids it. What may you do?
choices: Wait for the green light only
Turn left only on a green arrow

items.q: You may turn left on red from a two-way street onto another two-way street after stopping.

fact: For a left turn, signal and approach in the leftmost lane for your direction (on a two-lane road, move to the left side of your lane). Yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, then turn into the nearest lane going your way without cutting the corner.
why: This keeps your path predictable and out of the way of oncoming and straight-through traffic.

items.q: You are on a two-lane road and plan to turn left. Where should you position your car?
choices: On the left side of your lane
On the right side of your lane

items.q: When turning left, you should turn into the nearest lane going your direction without cutting the corner.

fact: At a steady red light, you may turn right after coming to a full stop and yielding to cross-traffic, unless a sign says not to.
why: A right turn on red does not cross oncoming lanes, so it can be done safely after a stop.

items.q: You are stopped at a steady red light and want to turn right. There is no sign about turning. Cross-traffic is clear. What may you do?
choices: Turn right after your full stop
Wait until the light turns green
Turn only if a green arrow appears

items.q: You may turn right on a steady red light without stopping if no cars are coming.
When is a right turn on a steady red NOT allowed in Idaho?
choices: On any street with two lanes

fact: For a right turn, signal and approach in the right lane close to the curb, watch for bicycles between you and the curb, and turn into the right lane of the new street without swinging wide.
why: Staying close to the curb and turning tightly keeps you out of other lanes and prevents cars from squeezing in on your right.

items.q: You are about to turn right. A bicycle is coming up on your right next to the curb. What should you do?
choices: Let the bicycle go first, then turn
Turn quickly ahead of the bicycle
Swing wide to the left to give space

items.q: After a right turn, which lane should you end up in?
choices: The right-hand lane of the cross street
The left lane of the cross street

fact: You may not make a U-turn on a curve or on or near the top of a hill where vehicles from either direction cannot see you within 500 feet.
why: Other drivers need time to see you and stop while your car is across the road.

items.q: A U-turn is illegal where approaching drivers cannot see your vehicle within how many feet?
You missed your turn and are near the top of a hill. Drivers coming over the hill could only see you about 200 feet away. May you make a U-turn here?
choices: No, drivers must be able to see you within 500 feet
Yes, if no cars are in sight right now

items.q: U-turns are allowed on curves as long as you signal.

fact: To make a U-turn: pull to the far right edge and stop, check ahead, behind, and your left-rear blind spot, then signal and turn sharply left while moving slowly. Recheck behind before speeding up to traffic speed.
why: Starting from the far right gives you the most room, and checking your blind spot catches cars you cannot see in mirrors.

items.q: What is the first step in making a U-turn on a two-lane road?
choices: Pull to the far right edge and stop

items.q: When making a U-turn, you should check your left-rear blind spot before turning.

fact: U-turns are not allowed where No U-turn signs are posted, in a no-passing zone, or where solid lines are painted in the center of the road. Stop and yield to all traffic before finishing a U-turn.
why: These are places where a car turning across the road is especially dangerous.

items.q: Where is a U-turn NOT allowed?
choices: On a straight road with clear views
On a road with a dashed center line

items.q: Solid pavement markings in the center of the road mean a U-turn is not allowed.

fact: When you stop behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see its rear tires where they touch the ground.
why: This space can keep you from being pushed into the car ahead if you are hit from behind, and lets you go around it if it stalls.
hook: Stopped in line? See their tires touching the road.

items.q: You stop behind a car at a red light. How much space should you leave?
choices: Enough to see its rear tires touching the ground
Enough to see its roof only

items.q: Why should you leave space when stopped behind another car?
choices: So you can go around it if it stalls
So you can back up quickly
So other cars can park there

fact: On two-lane roads, do not pass on or near hills, curves, or anything else that keeps you from seeing oncoming vehicles.
why: An oncoming car could appear with no time for either of you to avoid a head-on crash.

items.q: You are behind a slow tractor on a two-lane road, going up a hill. You cannot see over the top. What should you do?
choices: Wait until you can see far enough ahead to pass safely
Pass if the tractor waves you by

items.q: On a two-lane road, passing is not allowed on a hill or curve that blocks your view of oncoming traffic.

fact: Passing is not allowed within 100 feet of an intersection or a railroad crossing, unless traffic-control devices say otherwise.
why: Cars may turn or stop suddenly near intersections and crossings, and you would be in the wrong lane.
hook: 100 feet: no passing near intersections, railroad crossings, and blocked-view bridges or tunnels.

items.q: Within how many feet of an intersection is passing prohibited (unless signs or markings allow it)?
On a two-lane road, you are 80 feet from a railroad crossing behind a slow car. May you pass?
choices: No, passing is not allowed within 100 feet of a crossing
Yes, if no train is coming
Yes, if you finish before the tracks

items.q: You may pass another vehicle 50 feet before an intersection if no cars are coming.

fact: If you start to pass and decide you cannot finish safely, pull back into your lane behind the vehicle and wait for another chance.
why: Giving up on a pass is safer than forcing it into a head-on risk.

items.q: You start passing, then see an oncoming car closer than you thought. What should you do?
choices: Slow and pull back in behind the vehicle
Speed up and squeeze back in
Keep going and flash your lights

items.q: If you start to pass and cannot finish safely, you should pull back in behind the vehicle.

fact: Passing is not allowed within 100 feet of a bridge or tunnel when your view is blocked.
why: You cannot see oncoming traffic, and bridges and tunnels leave no room to escape.

items.q: On a two-lane road, you are 60 feet from a narrow bridge and a hill blocks your view of the far side. A slow car is ahead. May you pass?
choices: No, wait until you are past the bridge and can see
Yes, if you finish before the bridge
Yes, if the slow car moves right

items.q: Within how many feet of a bridge or tunnel with a blocked view is passing prohibited?
You may pass near a tunnel entrance as long as you finish the pass inside the tunnel.

fact: Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a marked or unmarked crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.
why: The stopped car can hide the person walking in front of it.

items.q: On a street with two lanes going your way, the car in the lane next to you stops at a crosswalk. You do not see why. What should you do?
choices: Stop too; a pedestrian may be crossing
Change lanes behind it and pass

items.q: You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

fact: Passing is not allowed when you would have to drive off the pavement or roadway to do it, and this includes passing on the right.
why: Shoulders are not built for traffic and may have people, bikes, debris, or soft edges.

items.q: The car ahead stops to turn left. The only way around it on the right is the gravel shoulder. What should you do?
choices: Pass on the left over the center line

items.q: It is legal to use the shoulder to pass a car that is turning left.

fact: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead on a two-lane road is signaling a left turn, or on a one-way or multi-lane road with two or more lanes going your way. Never leave the roadway to do it.
why: Drivers do not expect to be passed on the right, so it is allowed only where there is a proper lane for it.

items.q: On a two-lane, two-way road, the car ahead is stopped and signaling a left turn. There is a full lane-width of pavement to its right. May you pass on the right?
choices: Yes, if you can do it safely without leaving the roadway
No, passing on the right is never allowed

items.q: When is passing on the right allowed?
choices: On a road with two or more lanes going your direction
Whenever the car ahead is slow
When the right shoulder is paved

fact: After passing, wait until you can see the vehicle you passed in your rear-view mirror, then signal right and move back into the lane.
why: Seeing the car in your mirror means you have left enough room and will not cut it off.

items.q: When is it safe to return to the right lane after passing?
choices: When you can see the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
As soon as your front bumper is past it
When you are one car length ahead
When the other driver flashes the lights

items.q: After passing, you should be able to see the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror before moving back.

fact: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots because someone may be passing you, then signal left. If the car you are passing drifts toward you, use your horn.
why: Another car could already be in the passing lane, and the horn warns a driver who has not seen you.

items.q: What should you do if the vehicle you are passing begins to drift toward you?
choices: Brake hard in the passing lane

items.q: Before passing, you should check your blind spots in case someone is passing you.

fact: On a two-lane road, a passenger car, motorcycle, or pickup not towing anything may go up to 15 mph over the posted limit while passing a vehicle that is going below the limit.
why: A short burst of speed shortens the time you spend in the oncoming lane.

items.q: While passing on a two-lane road (when allowed), up to how many mph over the posted limit may a car go?
You are driving a car on a two-lane highway posted at 65 mph and are passing a truck going 55. What is the fastest you may go while passing?
You may use the passing speed exception while towing a trailer.

fact: The 15 mph passing exception applies only where the posted limit is 55 mph or higher, never in work zones, and you must return to your lane and slow to the limit as soon as you can.
why: Lower-speed roads and work zones have more hazards close to the road, so extra speed is not allowed there.

items.q: The passing speed exception only applies where the posted speed limit is at least how many mph?
You are passing a slow car on a two-lane road posted at 45 mph. May you go over 45 while passing?
choices: No, the exception only applies where the limit is 55 or more
Yes, as long as you signal

items.q: The passing speed exception also applies in work zones.

fact: When another vehicle is passing you, do not speed up. Keep a steady speed or slow down, and move to the right side of your lane.
why: Speeding up traps the passing driver in the oncoming lane.

items.q: A car starts to pass you on a two-lane road. What should you do?
choices: Keep a steady speed or slow down and move to the right of your lane
Speed up so it can't pass
Move to the left side of your lane

items.q: When being passed, you should speed up to help the other driver get by faster.

fact: On a multi-lane highway, do not pass a funeral procession on the right unless the procession is in the farthest left lane.
why: Passing on the right near the procession could interfere with its cars moving as a group.

items.q: On a multi-lane highway, a funeral procession is in the far left lane. May you pass it in a right lane?
choices: Yes, because it is in the farthest left lane
No, you may never pass a procession
Only if a police officer is present
Only if you use your hazard lights

items.q: You may always pass a funeral procession on the right on a multi-lane highway.

fact: Finish passing before you come within 200 feet of oncoming traffic, and before you reach a No Passing zone.
why: Both cars are moving toward each other quickly, so you need a large safety gap.

items.q: You must complete a pass before coming within how many feet of oncoming traffic?
How close may an oncoming vehicle be when you finish passing?

fact: A slow vehicle that is holding up three or more vehicles in a rural area or on a two-lane highway must pull off the road where it is safe to let them pass.
why: A long line behind a slow vehicle tempts drivers to make risky passes.

items.q: A slow vehicle on a two-lane highway must pull over to let others pass when it is delaying how many or more vehicles?
You are towing a heavy trailer slowly on a two-lane highway. Four cars are lined up behind you. What must you do?
choices: Pull off where it is safe to let them pass
Keep going; they can pass when they can
Speed up beyond what is safe
Turn on hazard lights and keep going

items.q: A slow vehicle only has to pull over when ten or more cars are behind it.

fact: To check following distance, pick a fixed object ahead, like a sign or tree. When the car ahead passes it, count three seconds. If you reach it before you finish counting, you are too close.
why: Counting time works at any speed, because the distance grows as you go faster.

items.q: The car ahead passes a road sign. You count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two' and you reach the sign. What does this mean?
choices: You are at a safe distance

items.q: When using the three-second rule, when do you start counting?
choices: When the car ahead passes a fixed object
When you pass the fixed object
When you see the car's brake lights

fact: Keep at least a three-second following distance behind the vehicle ahead. This is the minimum; increase it at high speeds or in bad weather.
why: You need time to notice the car ahead braking and then stop your own car.

items.q: What is the minimum recommended following distance, in seconds?
It is raining hard on the highway. How should you change your following distance?
choices: Increase it to more than three seconds
Keep it at exactly three seconds
Shorten it so you can see the car's taillights

items.q: Two seconds is the minimum safe following distance in good weather.

fact: Keep space around your car on all sides and stay in the middle of your lane. If someone follows you too closely, slow down and let them pass.
why: Space gives you time and room to react to danger; letting a tailgater pass removes the risk behind you.

items.q: A car is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What is the safest thing to do?
choices: Slow down and let it pass
Tap your brakes to warn it

items.q: If a car follows you too closely, you should slow down and let it pass.

fact: When parking on a public road, park parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb or road edge, facing the same direction as traffic on that side.
why: Parking close and with traffic keeps your car out of the travel lane and lets you pull out safely.

items.q: When parallel parking, you must be within how many inches of the curb?
You see an open spot on the left side of a two-way street, facing oncoming traffic. May you park there facing that way?
choices: No, you must face the same direction as traffic on that side
Yes, if you are within 18 inches of the curb
Yes, for less than an hour
Yes, if your hazard lights are on

items.q: You may park up to 24 inches from the curb.

fact: After parking, shift an automatic into park or leave a manual transmission in gear, remove the keys, and secure your car.
why: This keeps the car from rolling and from being stolen.

items.q: If your car has a manual transmission, how should you leave it when parked?
You should take the keys with you when you leave your parked car.

fact: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
why: If the car rolls, the wheels steer it into the curb or off the road instead of into traffic.

items.q: You park facing downhill next to a curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?
When parked facing downhill, you should turn your wheels toward the curb.

fact: When parking on a hill with no curb, uphill or downhill, turn your front wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.
why: If the car rolls, it will go off the road instead of into traffic.

items.q: You park facing uphill on a country road with no curb. Which way do you turn your wheels?
choices: Toward the edge of the road
Away from the edge of the road

items.q: With no curb, you turn your wheels toward the road edge whether you face uphill or downhill.

fact: When parking facing uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb and against it.
why: If the car rolls backward, the tire catches against the curb.
hook: Uphill with a curb: Up and away.

items.q: You park facing uphill next to a curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?
When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels toward the curb.

fact: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk.
why: Parked cars near a crosswalk hide people who are about to cross.

items.q: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
What is the closest you may park to a crosswalk?

fact: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway.
why: Fire trucks must be able to leave the station quickly with room to turn.

items.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire station driveway?
You may park 10 feet from a fire station driveway if you stay with your car.
What is the closest you may park to a fire station driveway?

fact: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
why: Firefighters need clear, quick access to the hydrant.

items.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
You find a parking spot that is about 10 feet from a fire hydrant. May you park there?
choices: No, you must be at least 15 feet away
Yes, more than 5 feet is fine
Yes, if you stay in the car

fact: Never park in bike lanes, on sidewalks, in intersections, on bridges or overpasses, in front of a driveway, on a freeway, or on the street side of a parked car (double parking).
why: A car in these places blocks others or creates a hazard that traffic cannot easily avoid.

items.q: What is 'double parking'?
choices: Parking on the street side of a parked car
Parking in two different lots in one day
Parking with two wheels on the curb

items.q: You need to drop off a package quickly. The only open space is in a bike lane. May you park there?
choices: No, parking in bike lanes is not allowed
Yes, if your hazard lights are on
Yes, if no bikes are in sight

items.q: You may park on a bridge if there is a wide shoulder.
You may park in a bike lane for a short time if no bicyclists are around.

fact: Do not park within 50 feet of railroad tracks.
why: A parked car near the tracks can block views of trains and could be hit.

items.q: You may not park within how many feet of railroad tracks?
What is the closest you may park to railroad tracks?

fact: Do not park where signs prohibit it or where the curb is painted red.
why: Red curbs and no-parking signs mark spots that must stay clear for safety or access.

items.q: What does a red-painted curb mean?
You may park at a red-painted curb at night.

fact: Do not park within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal.
why: Parked cars there would block drivers' view of the sign or signal.

items.q: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign?
How close to a traffic signal may you park?
You may park 20 feet from a yield sign.

fact: Only vehicles with a handicapped symbol on the license plate or a special card may park in handicapped spaces. Others may be fined.
why: These spaces are close to entrances for people who cannot walk far.

items.q: You are running into a store for one minute and the only open spot is a handicapped space. Your car has no plate or card. May you park there?
choices: No, and you may be fined
Yes, if you leave your hazard lights on
Yes, if someone stays in the car

items.q: A handicapped driver displaying the symbol may park in reserved spaces without paying and for unlimited time.

fact: An unattended vehicle on the paved shoulder (off the travel lanes) must be removed before dark, or it may be towed at the owner's expense.
why: At night, a car on the shoulder without lights is hard to see and can be hit.

items.q: Your car breaks down and you leave it on the paved shoulder of a highway. By when must it be moved?
If your unattended car on the shoulder is towed after dark, the state pays the towing cost.

fact: A vehicle left unattended on the traveled part of a highway may be towed away immediately, at any time.
why: A stopped car in a traffic lane is a serious danger to other drivers.

items.q: An unattended vehicle left in a highway travel lane can be towed right away.
What can happen to an unattended car left on the traveled part of a highway?
choices: It gets a warning note only

fact: Never park in or near an escape (runaway truck) ramp. These ramps are only for stopping vehicles whose brakes have failed.
why: A truck with no brakes may need the ramp at any moment.

items.q: It is fine to park in a runaway truck ramp to rest if it is empty.
What is a runaway truck ramp for?
choices: Stopping vehicles whose brakes have failed
Turning around on a steep hill

fact: Backing is always illegal on freeways, expressways, and other controlled-access highways, including the shoulder. If you miss your exit, go on to the next one.
why: Freeway traffic is fast and never expects a car moving backward.

items.q: You just passed your exit on the interstate. What should you do?
choices: Back up slowly on the shoulder
Turn around using the median crossover
Stop and wait for a gap to back up

items.q: Backing up is illegal even on the shoulder of a freeway.

fact: A freeway entrance usually has three parts: an entrance ramp, an acceleration lane, and a merging area. Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic.
why: Matching freeway speed lets you blend in smoothly without forcing others to brake.

items.q: What is the acceleration lane for?
choices: Speeding up to match freeway traffic
Stopping to wait for a gap

items.q: In the acceleration lane, you should speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

fact: Where designated and when weather permits, the speed limit may be up to 80 mph on rural interstates and up to 65 mph on urban interstates, unless otherwise posted.
why: Urban interstates have more entrances, exits, and traffic, so the limit is lower than in rural areas.

items.q: Where designated, up to what speed may you travel on an urban interstate, in mph?
Where designated, what is the highest speed allowed on a rural Idaho interstate?
Where designated, urban interstates allow the same top speed as rural interstates.

fact: Before a long freeway trip, make a travel plan with stops for food, rest, and fuel, and tell someone your route and when you expect to arrive. On short trips, know your route and your entrance and exit numbers.
why: Planning ahead prevents last-second decisions and helps people find you if something goes wrong.

items.q: Before a long freeway trip, what should your travel plan include?
choices: Stops for food, rest, and fuel
Only the speed limits on the route
Times when police are not patrolling

items.q: Before a long trip, it is a good idea to tell someone your route and when you expect to be back.

fact: When entering a freeway, signal, look over your left shoulder for a gap, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.
why: Freeway traffic is moving fast and has the right-of-way; you must fit into it.

items.q: You are merging onto the freeway. A car in the right lane is about to pass the end of your acceleration lane. Who must yield?
choices: You must yield to the car on the freeway
The car on the freeway must let you in

items.q: Drivers already on the freeway must yield to drivers entering from the ramp.

fact: If a short acceleration lane and heavy traffic force you to stop, leave room ahead so you can speed up, and wait for a gap large enough to reach freeway speed.
why: Without room to build speed, you would enter the freeway far too slowly.

items.q: Heavy traffic forces you to stop at the end of a short on-ramp. What should you do?
choices: Wait for a large gap, then speed up quickly to merge
Pull out slowly into the first small gap
Back up to try the ramp again
Drive on the shoulder until a gap opens

items.q: In heavy traffic, you may have to slow down before the end of the acceleration lane if there is no gap.

fact: If you take the wrong freeway entrance, never back up or turn around through the median. Freeway median crossovers are only for maintenance and emergency vehicles, so wait for the next exit to change direction.
why: Turning around or backing on a freeway puts you in the path of fast traffic.

items.q: You realize you are on the freeway going the wrong direction from where you want to go. You see a median crossover ahead. What should you do?
choices: Drive to the next exit and turn around there
Make a U-turn on the shoulder

items.q: Who may use freeway median crossovers?

fact: On a freeway, usually drive in the far right or center lane. The left lane is for faster traffic and passing. During rush hour, avoid the right lane to leave room for entering drivers.
why: Keeping the left lane open for passing and the right lane open for merging keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

items.q: What is the left lane of a freeway mainly used for?
It is rush hour on a three-lane freeway. You are not passing anyone and will not exit soon. Which lane is best?

fact: On the freeway, keep a steady speed with the flow of traffic. A minimum speed may be posted; if you cannot or will not drive the posted speed, use a different kind of road.
why: Big speed differences on a freeway lead to crashes and dangerous passing.

items.q: You are nervous at high speeds and want to drive 40 mph on a freeway where traffic goes 70. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Drive 40 mph in the right lane
Drive 40 mph with hazard lights on

items.q: Freeways may have a posted minimum speed.

fact: After you leave the exit ramp, the road you enter may have slower speeds and more complicated, dangerous traffic than the freeway. Stay alert and adjust to the new conditions.
why: After a long time at freeway speed, normal speeds can feel slow, and you may drive too fast without noticing.

items.q: Traffic on the road at the end of an exit ramp can be more complicated than freeway traffic.
What should you expect when you leave the freeway and enter another road?
choices: Slower speeds and more complicated traffic
The same speed limit as the freeway
Fewer hazards than on the freeway

fact: When exiting a freeway, signal and move into the deceleration lane, then slow down there, not in the main freeway lanes. If an exit speed is posted, adjust your speed to it on the ramp.
why: Slowing in the deceleration lane lets you lose speed without slowing the traffic behind you.

items.q: Where should you slow down when leaving a freeway?
choices: In the main freeway lane before the exit

items.q: You should brake hard in the freeway travel lane before moving into the exit lane.

fact: To leave a freeway, if you are not already in the correct lane, signal and move into the lane closest to the exit about half a mile before the exit.
why: Getting into the exit lane early keeps you from making a sudden lane change at the last second.

items.q: About how far before a freeway exit should you move into the lane nearest the exit, in miles?
You are in the left lane of a freeway and your exit is on the right in about half a mile. What should you do?
choices: Signal and move into the lane nearest the exit now
Stay in the left lane until you see the exit ramp
Cross all lanes at once when you reach the exit
Slow down in the left lane until traffic lets you over

items.q: It is safest to wait until you reach the exit ramp before moving over from the left lane.

fact: You must give your full attention to driving safely. If you do not, you can get a ticket for inattentive driving.
why: A driver who is not paying attention can miss hazards and cause a crash.

items.q: In Idaho, you can be cited for inattentive driving if you do not give full attention to driving.
What can happen if you do not give your full attention to driving?
choices: You can be cited for inattentive driving
Only a warning can be given

fact: It is illegal for passengers or cargo to block the driver's view or interfere with driving the vehicle.
why: The driver needs a clear view and free control to drive safely.

items.q: You stack boxes on the front passenger seat so high that you cannot see out the right side window. What is true?
choices: It is illegal because the cargo blocks your view
It is legal if the trip is short
It is legal during daylight hours
It is legal if you drive under 25 mph

items.q: A passenger may sit in a way that blocks the driver's view if the trip is short.

fact: Reckless driving, meaning driving with willful disregard for the safety of people or property, is illegal on public roads and on private property.
why: Dangerous driving can hurt people no matter where it happens.

items.q: You can be guilty of reckless driving even on private property.
Where does Idaho's reckless driving law apply?
choices: On public roads and private property

fact: In work zones, watch for hazards like uneven pavement, narrow lanes, heavy equipment, and gravel. Do not follow too closely, limit distractions such as a phone or the stereo, and remember workers may be just inches from traffic, day or night.
why: Speeding, inattention, failing to yield, and bad lane changes all add to crashes in work zones.

items.q: Which is good driving in a work zone?
choices: Leave plenty of space behind the car ahead
Follow closely to keep traffic moving
Change lanes often to find the fastest lane
Make a phone call while traffic is slow

items.q: Work zone workers are only present during the day, so you can relax at night.

fact: Before backing, check behind the vehicle before you get in. While backing, put your right arm on the passenger seat, look over your shoulder through the rear window instead of relying on mirrors, and back slowly.
why: Small children and objects are hard to see from the driver's seat, and a car is harder to control in reverse.

items.q: What is the best way to see while backing up?
choices: Look over your shoulder through the rear window
Open your door and lean out

items.q: When backing up, you should look over your shoulder through the rear window.

fact: Driver error causes more than 90% of highway crashes.
why: Most crashes come from choices and mistakes drivers make, so your own attention and habits matter most.

items.q: Driver error causes more than what percent of highway crashes?
What is the main cause of most highway crashes?
Most highway crashes are caused by vehicle breakdowns, not by driver error.

fact: The five steps for leaving the curb, parking, or changing lanes are: check mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder, move smoothly when safe, then cancel the signal.
why: Mirrors miss blind spots, so the shoulder check comes after the mirrors and before the move.

items.q: What is the first step before you change lanes?
What is the last step after you change lanes?
When changing lanes, you should glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

fact: When pulling away from the curb, into a parking space, or changing lanes, signal for five seconds or 100 feet before you move.
why: This gives other drivers enough time to see what you plan to do.

items.q: Before pulling away from the curb or changing lanes, how many seconds should you signal?
Before pulling away from the curb or changing lanes, you should signal for 5 seconds or how many feet?
How long should you signal before you change lanes?

fact: Before you get into your vehicle, look in front of it and behind it for children or objects you could run over.
why: Small children and low objects close to the car cannot be seen from the driver's seat.

items.q: What should you do before you get into your parked vehicle?
choices: Look in front of and behind it for children or objects
Start the engine with the remote to warm it up
Check the tire pressure with a gauge

items.q: Once you are in the driver's seat, you can easily see a small child sitting right behind your car.

fact: To start the car: with the parking brake set and the car in park or neutral, start the engine. Hold the foot brake, shift into gear, then release the parking brake.
why: Keeping the brakes on until you are in gear stops the car from rolling unexpectedly.

items.q: When you start the engine, what gear should the vehicle be in?
choices: Any gear, if the parking brake is on

items.q: You should release the parking brake before you start the engine.

fact: If you are upset, worried, or distracted, let someone else drive.
why: Strong emotions take your attention away from the road and make a crash far more likely.

items.q: You just had a big argument with a family member and you feel very angry. You need to go to the store. What is the safest choice?
choices: Drive fast to get it done quickly
Drive, but play loud music to calm down
Drive, but only on side streets

items.q: Over-confidence can make a driver more likely to crash.

fact: Give extra room to drivers who may not see you: drivers coming out of blocked driveways or intersections, drivers backing out, and drivers with ice or snow on their windows.
why: If they cannot see you, they may pull into your path.

items.q: You should give extra room to drivers who may not see you. Which driver is one of these?
choices: A driver backing out of a parking space
A driver who has already passed you and is far ahead
A driver behind you who is keeping a safe following distance
A driver waiting at a red light who just waved to you

items.q: You see a car with its windows still covered in frost waiting to pull out of a driveway. What should you do?
choices: Give it extra room and be ready to stop
Speed up to pass before it pulls out
Flash your high beams and keep going
Move closer to the driveway so the driver sees you

fact: Drive with your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, at about the 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions. Check your owner's manual if your car has airbags.
why: Hands on both sides let you steer quickly and smoothly in an emergency.

items.q: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
Driving with one hand at the top of the wheel is the best way to react to emergencies.

fact: If a driver is passing you as you near a curve, hill, or oncoming car, slow down and let them back into your lane quickly.
why: Helping the other driver finish the pass prevents a head-on crash.

items.q: A car is passing you as you both approach a hill, and an oncoming car appears. What should you do?
choices: Slow down so the passing car can get back in quickly
Speed up so the passing car cannot get in
Keep the same speed and stay in place

items.q: You should make room for a driver who is about to be forced into your lane by an obstacle or a lane ending.

fact: Look about 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. In the city, that is about one block.
why: Seeing problems early prevents last-minute lane changes, turns, and stops that cause crashes.

items.q: How far ahead should good drivers look?
choices: Only to the car directly in front

items.q: Looking 10 to 15 seconds ahead in city driving is about how many blocks?
In city driving, looking 10 to 15 seconds ahead equals about three blocks.

fact: Look to both sides when approaching any place where people, cars, or animals may cross. Do not rely on traffic lights or stop signs, because other drivers may run them.
why: A green light does not stop another driver from running the red.

items.q: Your light just turned green. What should you do before entering the intersection?
choices: Look to both sides for anyone running the light
Go right away because you have the green

items.q: If you have a green light, you do not need to look to the sides.

fact: Blind spots are areas near the left and right rear corners of your car that mirrors do not show. Before moving sideways, quickly turn your head to check them.
why: A car can be hidden next to you even when your mirrors look clear.

items.q: Where are your vehicle's blind spots?
choices: Near the left and right rear corners
Directly in front of the hood

items.q: You want to move into the right lane. Your mirrors look clear. What should you do next?
choices: Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot

items.q: If your mirrors are adjusted correctly, you never need to turn your head before changing lanes.

fact: Defensive driving steps: identify hazards, predict what could happen (assume the worst), decide what to do ahead of time, and execute smoothly.
why: Making a decision early is safer than reacting at the last second.

items.q: You see children playing on a street corner ahead. According to defensive driving, what should you predict?
choices: One of them may run in front of you
They will stay on the corner
They will cross only at the light

items.q: What is the key to defensive driving?
choices: Making a sound decision ahead of time
Reacting quickly at the last second

items.q: When you spot a possible hazard, it is safest to predict the worst outcome.

fact: Check the traffic behind you several times a minute. Most rear-end collisions are caused by vehicles following too closely.
why: Knowing what is behind you tells you if someone is tailgating or coming up too fast.

items.q: How often should you check traffic behind you?
What causes most rear-end collisions?

fact: Avoid driving in another driver's blind spot.
why: It is as important for other drivers to see you as it is for you to see them.

items.q: You notice you have been driving just behind and to the side of another car for a while. What should you do?
choices: Speed up or drop back so you are not in its blind spot
Stay there because it is a safe spot
Honk so the driver knows you are there

items.q: Driving alongside another car's rear corner is a safe place to stay.

fact: Anything that takes your attention from the road is a distraction, such as using a phone, eating, reading, changing the radio, applying makeup, looking for items, or dealing with children or pets.
why: Even a few seconds of distraction can make you miss a child, a bicycle, or a car braking ahead.

items.q: Which of these is a driving distraction?
choices: Looking for something inside your car

items.q: A distraction of only a few seconds is too short to cause a crash.

fact: Prevent distractions by setting radio stations and planning your route before you drive, not eating while driving, and putting pets in a carrier.
why: Doing these things before you move keeps your eyes and hands free for driving.

items.q: When should you set your favorite radio stations?
choices: While a passenger holds the wheel

items.q: You are taking your dog to the vet alone. What is the best way to keep the dog from distracting you?
choices: Put the dog in a pet carrier
Let the dog sit on your lap
Let the dog ride loose in the back
Hold the leash while you drive

fact: Keep the stereo low enough to hear sounds outside the car, like sirens, horns, and screeching tires.
